{{Short description|Applications of category theory}}
'''Applied category theory''' is an [[Discipline (academia)|academic discipline]] in which methods from [[category theory]] are used to study other fields<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/mathematics/18-s097-applied-category-theory-january-iap-2019/|title=Applied Category Theory|website=MIT OpenCourseWare|access-date=2019-07-20}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|title=An Invitation to Applied Category Theory by Brendan Fong|last1=Spivak|first1=David I.|last2=Fong|first2=Brendan|date=July 2019|doi=10.1017/9781108668804|isbn=978-1-108-66880-4|s2cid=199139551}}</ref><ref>{{Cite arXiv|last=Bradley|first=Tai-Danae|date=2018-09-16|title=What is Applied Category Theory?|class=math.CT|eprint=1809.05923v2}}</ref> including but not limited to [[computer science]],<ref>{{Cite book|title=Category theory for computing science|last=Barr, Michael.|author-link = Michael Barr (mathematician)|date=1990|publisher=Prentice Hall|others=Wells, Charles.|isbn=0-13-120486-6|location=New York|oclc=19126000}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Ehrig|first1=Hartmut| The application of category theory in these domains can take different forms. In some cases the formalization of the domain into the language of category theory is the goal, the idea here being that this would elucidate the important structure and properties of the domain. In other cases the formalization is used to leverage the power of abstraction in order to prove new results or to develop new algorithms about the field.
